newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees arabica shortfall supporting prices.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees arabica shortfall supporting prices.

text.p: Colombia's top coffee official said record-low consumer inventories, and an arabica shortfall of up to 3 million 60-kg bags, should provide near-term support for the recent increase in world coffee prices.
Jorge Cardenas, head of Colombia's National Coffee Federation, gave his upbeat assessment to reporters after the federation's first regular policy-making meeting this year.

Underscoring his confidence about higher coffee prices, the meeting adjourned with an announcement that Colombia was raising its internal coffee price by 12 percent to 248,125 pesos per 125- kg load effective immediately.
"Fortunately, for coffee growers and the coffee economy, there's been a big change in the world market over the past few weeks," Cardenas said.

"The forecasts that we were working with up until the last day of December, regarding crops and coffee supply, have changed in the last few weeks due to very particular events in Brazil that had gone undetected," he said.
"The production situation has fallen a lot," he added, referring to Brazil and what he described as lower output from Colombia and Central America as well.

Cardenas said there was currently a deficit of arabica ranging anywhere between 2 million and 3 million 60-kg bags on world markets. That, coupled with what he described record-low inventories in consumer countries totaling no more than 7.8 million 60-kg bags, should provide fundamental near-term support for coffee, he said.
"The world has been working with such low inventories that it doesn't have, at the moment, any sort of a cushion against the supply situation and the rise in coffee prices," Cardenas said.
He said Colombia was expected to produce no more than about 2.6 million 60-kg bags of coffee between January and March.
He gave no comparative figure for the same period last year, but said production would increase between April and July to 4 million or 5 million 60-kg bags.
